1.title: When I was a child
1.brief: Write an email to a new friend from another country about your childhood. Describe where you lived, what you used to do and one thing you didn't use to like.
1.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo extranjero sobre tu infancia: dónde vivías, qué solías hacer y algo que no te gustaba.
criteria: Three affirmative “used to” sentences and one negative (didn’t use to).
Two words from the unit: childhood, back then, memory, ago.
A friendly greeting, two paragraphs and a closing.
1.model:
Hi Olivia,

You asked me about my childhood, so here it is! When I was a child, I lived on a farm near Armenia. Back then, we didn't have internet, so I used to play outside all day. My brother and I used to climb trees and we used to help my grandfather with the coffee plants.

I didn't use to like school because it was far away: I walked for an hour every morning! My best memory is the smell of coffee in the kitchen. What about you?

Hugs,
Mateo

1.title: The day everything changed
1.brief: Write a short story about a day when something surprising happened. Use the simple past to tell the events in order.
1.briefEs: Escribe una historia corta sobre un día en que pasó algo sorprendente, en pasado simple.
criteria: Eight verbs in the simple past, at least four irregular.
Use “suddenly” and “at the time”.
One sentence with “was / were” to set the scene.
1.model: It was a normal Tuesday in 2019. I was 15 and I was at school. At the time, I didn't know anything about my father's plans. When I got home, my parents were in the kitchen with a big map. Suddenly, my father said, “We're moving to Canada!” I didn't believe him. I cried and I called my best friend. Two months later, we took a plane to Toronto. That day changed my life, and now I'm happy it happened.

1.title: A social media post: then and now
1.brief: Write a post for social media with an old photo. Compare how things used to be and how they are now.
1.briefEs: Escribe una publicación para redes con una foto antigua comparando cómo eran las cosas y cómo son ahora.
criteria: Two “used to” sentences and two present simple sentences.
Use “ago” correctly (ten years ago).
Include “to quit” or “to move (house)”.
1.model: #ThrowbackThursday This photo is from fifteen years ago! I used to have very long hair and I used to wear huge glasses. I used to play the violin, but I quit when I was twelve. We used to live in Cúcuta, but we moved house to Bogotá in 2015. Now I have short hair and I wear contact lenses. I don't play the violin anymore, but I sing in a choir. Do you remember me like this?

1.title: Remember our street?
1.brief: Write a message to an old friend about the street where you both played as children. Say what you used to do there and one thing you didn't use to like.
1.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un viejo amigo sobre la calle donde jugaban de niños: qué solían hacer allí y qué cosa no les gustaba.
criteria: Two affirmative “used to” sentences and one “didn’t use to” sentence.
Use “back then” once and one time expression with a year or “ago”.
Ask your friend one question with “Did you use to…?”.
1.model:
Hi Tomás!

I found an old photo of our street today. Do you remember it? Back then, we used to play football there every afternoon. The shop on the corner used to sell ice cream for very little money. I didn't use to like the old bakery, but now I miss its bread! We moved to another city in 2012. Did you use to visit the street after that? Send me a photo of it now!

Cheers,
Nico

1.title: Questions for my grandad
1.brief: Write a short conversation between you and your grandad about his life when he was young. Use questions about his habits and about one thing that changed.
1.briefEs: Escribe una conversación corta con tu abuelo sobre cómo era su vida de joven: sus costumbres y algo que cambió.
criteria: Three questions: two with “Did you use to…?” and one with “What happened…?”.
Short answers with “Yes, I did.” or “No, I didn’t.”.
At least one answer with “used to” and one with a year.
1.model:
Did you use to walk to school, Grandad?
Yes, I did. It took one hour!
Did you use to have a phone?
No, I didn't. We used to write letters.
What happened to your old school?
They closed it in 1990.

1.title: The bus that stopped
1.brief: Write a diary entry about a day when something went wrong on the way to school or work. Tell the events in order in the simple past.
1.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario sobre un día en que algo salió mal camino al colegio o al trabajo, contando los hechos en pasado simple.
criteria: Six verbs in the simple past, at least three of them irregular.
Use “suddenly” once and “noticed” once.
Start with a date line and end with a short sentence about how you feel.
1.model:
Tuesday, 14 May

Today was a strange day. I got on the bus at seven and I sat next to the window. Suddenly, the bus stopped in the middle of the road. The driver got out and looked at the engine. Then I noticed that my phone was dead, so I could not call my mum. We waited for forty minutes. At last, another bus arrived. I was late for school, but my teacher wasn't angry. I'm tired now. Goodnight!

1.title: Why I quit playing at night
1.brief: Write a short opinion about a habit you quit. Say how your life was before and how it is now.
1.briefEs: Escribe una opinión breve sobre un hábito que dejaste: cómo era tu vida antes y cómo es ahora.
criteria: Use “quit” and “ago” correctly.
One “used to” sentence and one “didn’t use to” sentence.
Give your opinion with “In my opinion…”.
1.model: I quit playing video games at night six months ago. I used to play until two in the morning, so I was always tired at school. I didn't use to do any exercise either. Back then, I thought games were more important than sleep. Now I go to bed at eleven, and I run with my brother on Saturdays. It wasn't easy at the time, but I feel much better. In my opinion, sleep is better than any game.

1.title: Goodbye, old flat
1.brief: You moved out of a flat last week. Write a short letter to the landlady to thank her and to remember your time there.
1.briefEs: Te mudaste de un apartamento la semana pasada. Escribe una carta corta a la propietaria para agradecerle y recordar tu tiempo allí.
criteria: Use “ago”, “at the time” and “moved out” once each.
One “used to” sentence and one negative sentence in the simple past.
A formal greeting, a thank-you and a closing.
1.model:
Dear Mrs Vega,

Thank you for everything. I moved out of the flat last Friday, and I left the keys in the kitchen. I have good memories of the place. Two years ago, I arrived with only two bags. At the time, I didn't know anyone in the city. Then I noticed how kind my neighbours were. I used to read on the small balcony every evening. I will miss it. Please say hello to your family.

Best wishes,
Hugo Salazar

1.title: Lost bag report
1.brief: You lost your backpack on a bus. Complete the report with full sentences: what happened, where, when and what was inside.
1.briefEs: Perdiste tu mochila en un autobús. Completa el reporte con oraciones completas: qué pasó, dónde, cuándo y qué había dentro.
criteria: Answer what, where and when with at least five verbs in the simple past.
Use “noticed” once and one negative past sentence (didn’t / wasn’t).
Give a phone number and a polite request.
1.model: I lost my blue backpack yesterday afternoon. I was on the number twelve bus from the stadium to the city centre. I got off at four o'clock, and then I noticed that the backpack wasn't with me. It contained a laptop, a notebook and my keys. I asked the driver, but he didn't see it. Please call me on 555 0198.

1.title: Mum and Dad in 1995
1.brief: Describe an old photo of your parents (or two people you know) when they were young. Say what they used to do and what they didn't use to do.
1.briefEs: Describe una foto antigua de tus padres (o de dos personas que conozcas) cuando eran jóvenes: qué solían hacer y qué no.
criteria: Two affirmative “used to” sentences and one “didn’t use to” sentence.
Use “was / were” at least twice.
One sentence in the present continuous about what you can see in the photo.
1.model: This photo is from 1995. My parents were twenty then, and they were students in Quito. My dad had long hair, and he used to wear big glasses. My mum used to ride a red bike to university. They didn't use to cook at home, so they often ate in cheap cafés. In the photo, they are laughing at something funny. I love this picture because they look very happy.

2.title: Shopping list for a party
2.brief: You are organising a party with a roommate. Write a message saying what you have, what you need and how much or how many.
2.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a tu compañero de cuarto sobre lo que tienen y lo que falta para una fiesta.
criteria: Use “a few / a little / a lot of / plenty of” correctly with count and noncount nouns.
Use “enough” and “not enough” once each.
Use “run out of” once.
2.model: Hi Juli! I checked the kitchen for the party. We have plenty of glasses and a lot of plates, but we don't have enough chairs. There's a little rice but not enough for twenty people, so please buy two kilos. We've run out of sugar and we only have a few lemons. There isn't much ice either. Can you buy a couple of bags? I'll buy the drinks and a few snacks.

2.title: Asking politely at a hotel
2.brief: Write an email to a hotel before your trip. Ask for information using indirect questions.
2.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un hotel pidiendo información con preguntas indirectas.
criteria: Four indirect questions (Could you tell me…? I'd like to know…).
Statement word order inside each question (where the station is).
Use “whether” or “if” once.
2.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am planning to stay at your hotel from 12 to 15 May. Could you tell me how much a double room costs? I would like to know whether breakfast is included. I was wondering if you have a room with a view of the sea. Do you know how far the hotel is from the airport? Could you also tell me what time check-in is?

Thank you for your help.

Kind regards,
Paola Herrera

2.title: What's in my fridge
2.brief: Describe what is in your fridge and kitchen today. Say what you have a lot of, a little of and what you need to buy.
2.briefEs: Describe qué hay hoy en tu nevera y cocina, y qué necesitas comprar.
criteria: Five different expressions of quantity.
No plural for noncount nouns (no “breads”, “milks”).
Use “container”, “quantity” or “a couple of”.
2.model: My fridge is almost empty today! There is a little milk and a couple of eggs. There are a few tomatoes, but there isn't any cheese. I have a big container of soup from yesterday — plenty for two people. In the cupboard there is a lot of rice and some pasta, but there isn't much coffee. I need to buy fruit, bread and more coffee. I can't live without coffee!

2.title: Biscuits for the bake sale
2.brief: Write a simple recipe for a school bake sale. Say what ingredients and how much of each you need, and explain the steps.
2.briefEs: Escribe una receta sencilla para una venta de pasteles del colegio: ingredientes, cantidades y pasos.
criteria: Four quantity expressions: a little, a few, a couple of, plenty of.
Use “enough” once and one container (a bag of, a bottle of).
Steps in the imperative (Put, Add, Mix…).
2.model:
Chocolate biscuits

You need a bag of flour, a little sugar and a couple of eggs. Put the flour in a big bowl. Add the sugar and mix it well. Break the eggs and add a few pieces of chocolate. Make small balls with your hands and put them on a tray. Bake them for twelve minutes. Leave plenty of space between the biscuits. Is there enough for everybody? Make a few more if you need them!

2.title: At the station in Madrid
2.brief: You are at Atocha station in Madrid. Write a short conversation with a staff member and ask for information politely.
2.briefEs: Estás en la estación de Atocha en Madrid. Escribe una conversación corta con un empleado pidiendo información con cortesía.
criteria: Three indirect questions with “Could you tell me…?” or “Do you know…?”.
Statement word order after the question word (where the ticket office is).
Short answers from the staff member.
2.model:
Excuse me, could you tell me where the ticket office is?
It's next to the café.
Thanks. Do you know what time the next train leaves?
At ten past nine.
Could you tell me how much a ticket costs?
It costs twelve euros.

2.title: The school canteen
2.brief: Write a review of your school canteen. Say what there is and what there isn't, and give a star rating.
2.briefEs: Escribe una reseña del comedor de tu colegio: qué hay, qué falta y cuántas estrellas le das.
criteria: Use “a lot of”, “enough” and “plenty of” once each.
One “not many” with a count noun and one “not much” with a noncount noun.
Give a star rating and one recommendation.
2.model: The food is cheap, but the portions are small. There are a lot of students at lunch, so we wait twenty minutes. There aren't enough tables, and there aren't many vegetables. There isn't much choice on Fridays either. On the good side, there is plenty of fruit and the staff are friendly. I think the canteen needs more tables and a little more variety. I give it three stars.

2.title: Kitchen notes for a new flatmate
2.brief: A new flatmate arrives today. Write a note about what there is in the kitchen and what you need.
2.briefEs: Hoy llega un compañero de piso nuevo. Escribe una nota sobre lo que hay en la cocina y lo que hace falta.
criteria: Use “run out of” once.
Three different expressions of quantity (plenty of, a little, many, much, a few).
One polite request with “Could you…?”.
2.model:
Hi Marta!

Welcome to the flat. There is plenty of rice and a little oil in the cupboard, so please use them. There aren't many clean plates, so wash yours after dinner. We have run out of coffee, but I'm buying some this afternoon. The fridge is small, so only keep a few things on your shelf. There isn't much space for bikes in the hall. Could you leave yours in the garage? Thanks a lot!

Lucía

2.title: Do students have enough free time?
2.brief: Give your opinion: do teenagers have enough free time? Use quantity expressions to explain.
2.briefEs: Da tu opinión: ¿tienen los adolescentes suficiente tiempo libre? Usa expresiones de cantidad.
criteria: Use “enough” and “a lot of” once each.
Use “a few” and “a little” once each.
Give your opinion with “In my opinion…” and one suggestion.
2.model: I think teenagers don't have enough free time. We have a lot of homework, and we spend six hours at school. There isn't much time for sports or friends. Some people have only a little time after dinner. A few students have extra classes too, so they are very tired. In my opinion, schools should give less homework. Then we will have plenty of time to rest and enjoy our hobbies.

2.title: Questions for a famous chef
2.brief: You are a journalist and you are going to interview a famous chef. Write four polite indirect questions.
2.briefEs: Eres periodista y vas a entrevistar a un chef famoso. Escribe cuatro preguntas indirectas y corteses.
criteria: Four indirect questions with different introducers (Could you tell me…, I’d like to know…, Do you know…, I wonder if…).
Statement word order after the question word.
Use “how many” or “how much” once.
2.model:
Could you tell me where you learned to cook?
I'd like to know how many hours you work every day.
Do you know what the most popular dish in your restaurant is?
I wonder if you ever run out of ideas.

2.title: Market day
2.brief: Write a diary entry about a trip to a street market in Cusco. Say what you bought, how much and what you paid in soles.
2.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario sobre una visita a un mercado de Cusco: qué compraste, cuánto y cuánto pagaste en soles.
criteria: Four quantity expressions (a lot of, a couple of, plenty of, enough…).
One container (a bag of) and one price in soles.
Use “enough” in a negative sentence.
2.model:
Saturday

Today I went to the market in Cusco with my aunt. We bought a lot of fruit, a bag of potatoes and a couple of kilos of tomatoes. The woman at the stall had plenty of cheap oranges, so we took ten. They cost only four soles! We didn't have enough bags, so my aunt asked a man if he could sell us two more. At home we saw that we didn't have any rice. Tomorrow I will buy some.

3.title: My flat: good and bad
3.brief: Describe your home. Evaluate it with adjectives and nouns (too small, not big enough, enough space) and say what you wish was different.
3.briefEs: Describe tu vivienda evaluándola (too, enough) y di qué desearías que fuera diferente.
criteria: Use “too + adjective” and “not + adjective + enough”.
Use “enough + noun” once.
Two wishes with “I wish + past simple / could”.
3.model: I live in a small flat in Medellín. It's very convenient because it's near the metro, but it's too noisy at night. The kitchen isn't big enough for a table, and there isn't enough space for my bike. On the good side, the rent is decent and the neighbours are friendly. I wish I had a balcony with plants. I wish the walls were thicker! And I wish I could have a dog, but the building doesn't allow pets.

3.title: A complaint about a hostel
3.brief: Write an online review of a place you didn't like (a hostel, a restaurant, a gym). Explain the drawbacks.
3.briefEs: Escribe una reseña en línea de un lugar que no te gustó y explica sus desventajas.
criteria: Three evaluations with too / enough / as… as.
Use “to complain”, “drawback” and “crowded”.
One wish about the place.
3.model:
Hostel Sol, Cartagena ★★
I stayed here for three nights and I have to complain. The location is great, but that's the only good thing. The rooms are too small and too hot, and there aren't enough fans. The bathroom isn't as clean as the photos show. The biggest drawback is the noise: the bar is very crowded until 2 a.m. I wish the staff were more helpful. I put up with it because it was cheap, but I won't go back.

3.title: If only…
3.brief: Write about three things in your life that you would like to change. Use wishes and explain why.
3.briefEs: Escribe tres cosas de tu vida que te gustaría cambiar usando “I wish” y explica por qué.
criteria: Three wishes with “I wish + past simple” or “could”.
Use “because” to give a reason for each wish.
Use one phrasal expression: put up with, settle for.
3.model: I'm quite happy, but there are three things I wish were different. First, I wish I lived closer to work because I spend two hours on the bus every day. Second, I wish I could speak English fluently, because I want to travel. Third, I wish my brother didn't play loud music: I have to put up with it every night! For now, I settle for headphones and patience.

3.title: Which home would you rent?
3.brief: Look at the house and the apartment in Unit 3 (rent, utilities, stratum, bedrooms, bathrooms and what each one has). Write an email to a friend who is moving to your city. Compare the two homes and recommend one.
3.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo comparando la casa y el apartamento de la unidad y recomiéndale uno.
criteria: Use at least four comparatives (cheaper, bigger, more expensive, better…).
Use “not as … as” once.
Use real numbers from the cards (prices, bedrooms…).
End with a clear recommendation: I think you should…
3.model:
Hi Laura,

I found two homes for you. The house costs COP 2,800,000 a month, and the apartment costs COP 1,600,000, so the apartment is much cheaper. The house is bigger: it has three bedrooms, but the apartment has only two. They both have two bathrooms. The apartment is in stratum 4 and the house is in stratum 3, but the apartment's utilities are lower: COP 280,000 a month. The house has a garden and a garage, and the apartment has a gym and a pool. The apartment isn't as quiet as the house, but it's closer to the city centre. I think you should rent the apartment because you live alone.

Love,
Camila

3.title: A note to a noisy neighbour
3.brief: Your neighbour plays loud music at night. Write a polite note to ask for a change.
3.briefEs: Tu vecino pone música alta por la noche. Escribe una nota cortés pidiendo un cambio.
criteria: One “too + adjective” and one “not + adjective + enough”.
One wish with “I wish + could / past simple”.
Use “noise” and “put up with”.
3.model:
Dear neighbour,

I'm writing about the noise at night. Your music is too loud after eleven, and the walls aren't thick enough. I can't sleep, and I have an exam this week. I know you like music, and I don't want to be rude. I wish you could use headphones after ten. I can put up with the noise in the afternoon, but not at night. Thank you for understanding.

Kind regards,
Mariana, flat 4B

3.title: Which gym should I join?
3.brief: You are choosing between two gyms in Lima. Compare them and explain your decision. Use prices in soles.
3.briefEs: Debes elegir entre dos gimnasios en Lima. Compáralos y explica tu decisión. Usa precios en soles.
criteria: One “as … as” sentence and one comparative with “than”.
Use “enough” once and “too” once.
Give a final decision with a reason (settle for / decent).
3.model: I think Fit Centre is better than Gym Sur. It isn't as expensive as Gym Sur: it costs 120 soles a month, and the other one costs 180. Fit Centre is also close enough to walk from my flat. However, it's too crowded in the evening, and there aren't enough machines. Gym Sur has more space, but it isn't as convenient as Fit Centre. In the end, I will settle for Fit Centre because the price is decent.

3.title: My city: wishes
3.brief: Write a social media post with things you wish were different in your city.
3.briefEs: Escribe una publicación para redes con cosas que te gustaría que fueran diferentes en tu ciudad.
criteria: Four wishes with “I wish + past simple / were / could”.
One “too” and one “not enough”.
Ask your followers a question and add a hashtag.
3.model: I love my city, but I have a few wishes. I wish the buses were more frequent because I wait too long every morning. I wish the streets were cleaner, and I wish we had more green spaces. The centre is too crowded at weekends, and there aren't enough bike lanes. I wish I could cycle to university safely. Do you agree? What do you wish for your city? #MyCity

3.title: Viewing a flat
3.brief: You are viewing a flat in Mexico City. Write a short conversation with the agent about size and rent in pesos.
3.briefEs: Estás viendo un apartamento en Ciudad de México. Escribe una conversación corta con el agente sobre el tamaño y el alquiler en pesos.
criteria: One “big enough” or “not … enough” and one “too + adjective”.
One wish with “I wish it were…”.
Ask about the price and answer in pesos.
3.model:
Is the flat big enough for two people?
It's just about big enough. The bedroom is small.
How much is the rent?
It's twelve thousand pesos a month.
That's too expensive for me. I wish it were cheaper.
I know, but it's in a very convenient place.

3.title: Too hot to study
3.brief: Your classroom is too hot and too noisy. Write a formal email to the school director.
3.briefEs: Tu salón es demasiado caluroso y ruidoso. Escribe un correo formal a la directora del colegio.
criteria: Two “too + adjective” and one “not + adjective + enough”.
Use “enough + noun” once.
One wish and one polite request with “Could you…?”.
3.model:
Dear Ms Ortega,

I am writing about classroom 12. The room is too hot in the afternoon, and the windows aren't big enough. There aren't enough fans, so many students feel tired and cannot work well. The classroom is also too noisy because it is next to the sports field. I wish we could change rooms. Could you please look into the problem? We can put up with it for a week, but not longer.

Yours sincerely,
Martín Ruiz, Year 10

3.title: I wish I hadn't…
3.brief: Write a diary entry about a day when you made some mistakes. Say what you wish you had done differently.
3.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario sobre un día en que cometiste errores y qué desearías haber hecho distinto.
criteria: Three regrets with “I wish + past perfect”.
One “too” and one “not … enough”.
Start with how you feel and end with a plan (Next time, I will…).
3.model:
Sunday night

I feel terrible today. I wish I hadn't stayed up until three in the morning. I wish I had gone to bed early, because my exam was at nine. I was too tired to think, and my answers weren't good enough. I also wish I had studied more last week. I wish I hadn't lost my notes! Next time, I will plan better. I just hope the result isn't too bad.

4.title: How I learned to cook
4.brief: Tell the story of how you learned something (to cook, to drive, to swim). Use sequence adverbs to order the steps.
4.briefEs: Cuenta cómo aprendiste algo (cocinar, manejar, nadar) usando adverbios de secuencia.
criteria: Use first, then, after that, next and finally.
The story is in the simple past.
One closing sentence in the present perfect (Since then, I have…).
4.model: I learned to cook when I was 18. First, my grandmother taught me to make rice. It was a disaster! Then I tried simple things like eggs and soup. After that, I looked up recipes online and practised every weekend. Next, I cooked a full lunch for my family on my mom's birthday. Finally, my grandmother said, “Now you are a real cook.” Since then, I have cooked hundreds of meals, and I have never burnt the rice again.

4.title: My experiences so far
4.brief: Write an email to a friend about your first month in a new job or course. Say what you have done so far and what you haven't done yet.
4.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo sobre tu primer mes en un trabajo o curso: lo que has hecho y lo que aún no.
criteria: Four sentences in the present perfect with so far, already, yet, recently.
One sentence in the simple past with a finished time (last Monday).
Use “since” or “for” once.
4.model:
Hi Manu,

I've been at my new job for a month now and I love it! So far, I have met all my team and I have already finished my first project. Recently, I have started to take the bike to work. Last Monday I gave my first presentation. I was nervous, but it went well. I haven't met the big boss yet and I haven't got my first salary yet!

Write soon,
Isa

4.title: A biography in steps
4.brief: Write a short biography of a famous Colombian or a member of your family. Say what they achieved, in order.
4.briefEs: Escribe una biografía corta de un colombiano famoso o un familiar, contando sus logros en orden.
criteria: Simple past for finished events with dates.
Present perfect for life achievements up to now (has won, has written).
Three sequence adverbs.
4.model: Mariana Pajón is a famous Colombian BMX rider. She was born in Medellín in 1991. First, she started riding bikes when she was four. Then she won her first world championship as a teenager. After that, she won a gold medal at the London Olympics in 2012, and she won another one in Rio in 2016. Next, she got silver in Tokyo. Up to now, she has won more than ten world titles and she has become a role model for many young athletes.

4.title: Have you ever…?
4.brief: Write a short chat with a friend about experiences. Ask about things you have done and then about the details.
4.briefEs: Escribe un chat corto con un amigo sobre experiencias: pregunta qué ha hecho y luego los detalles.
criteria: Two questions with “Have you ever…?” and short answers (Yes, I have. / No, I haven’t.).
Two details in the simple past with a finished time (last year, in July).
Use “What was it like?” once.
4.model:
Have you ever been to the beach?
Yes, I have. I went to Santa Marta last year.
Have you ever tried surfing?
No, I haven't. Have you?
Yes, I have. I tried it in July.
What was it like?
It was great, but I fell a lot!

4.title: A letter for a summer job
4.brief: Write a short letter to apply for a summer job in a bike shop. Say what experience you have.
4.briefEs: Escribe una carta corta para pedir un trabajo de verano en una tienda de bicicletas, contando tu experiencia.
criteria: Three present perfect sentences with for, never, already or so far.
One simple past sentence with a finished time (last summer).
A formal greeting and closing.
4.model:
Dear Mr Duarte,

I am writing about the summer job at your bike shop. I have worked in a shop for two years, so I already know how to help customers. Last summer, I repaired bikes at my uncle's garage, and I learned a lot. I have never worked with children, but I have taught my little sister to ride. So far, I have not used your repair software, but I learn quickly. I am free from June. Thank you for reading my letter.

Yours sincerely,
Carla Núñez

4.title: How to change your Wi-Fi password
4.brief: Explain to a friend how to change the Wi-Fi password at home. Put the steps in order.
4.briefEs: Explica a un amigo cómo cambiar la clave del wifi de casa, con los pasos en orden.
criteria: Use first, then, next, after that and finally in order.
Steps in the imperative.
One present perfect sentence with “yet” or “this year”.
4.model: First, open your browser and type the router address. Then enter the user name and the password from the back of the router. Next, click on Wi-Fi settings. After that, delete the old password and write a new one with letters and numbers. Finally, save the changes and connect your phone again. I have changed my password twice this year, and I haven't had any problems yet.

4.title: A review of an English app
4.brief: Write a review of an app you have used to learn English. Say how long you have used it and what has happened so far.
4.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una aplicación que usaste para aprender inglés: cuánto tiempo la usas y qué ha pasado hasta ahora.
criteria: Use “for” and “since” once each with the present perfect.
Use “so far”, “already” and “recently”.
One simple past sentence with a finished time (Yesterday…) and a star rating.
4.model: I have used this English app for three months, and I really like it. Since I started, I have learned about 400 new words. Yesterday I finished level five, and I got a badge! So far, I haven't found any big problems. The only drawback is that I have already seen some of the exercises twice. Recently, they have added short stories, which is great. I recommend it to every beginner. Four stars!

4.title: Late homework
4.brief: Write an email to a teacher to explain the state of your project and ask for more time.
4.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un profesor explicando cómo va tu proyecto y pidiendo más tiempo.
criteria: Use “already” and “yet” once each.
Use “since” and “for” with the present perfect.
One simple past sentence with a finished time (on Monday).
4.model:
Dear Mr Hill,

I am writing about the history project. I have already finished the first two parts, and I sent you the photos on Monday. I haven't written the conclusion yet because I have been ill since Tuesday. Could I send it on Friday instead? I have worked on this project for three weeks, so I want to finish it well. Thank you for your help.

Best wishes,
Samuel

4.title: Backpacking update
4.brief: Write a social media post about your trip in Peru so far. Say what you have done and what you haven't done yet.
4.briefEs: Escribe una publicación sobre tu viaje por Perú hasta ahora: qué has hecho y qué aún no.
criteria: Two present perfect sentences with so far, yet or since.
One simple past sentence with a finished time (On Monday…).
At least three sequence adverbs (first, then, next, finally).
4.model: Day five in Peru! So far, I have visited Lima and Cusco. On Monday, I took a bus to Cusco, and the views were amazing. First, I walked around the main square. Then I tried guinea pig, and it was interesting! I haven't seen Machu Picchu yet, but I'm going there tomorrow. I have met many nice travellers since I arrived. Next, I will go to Arequipa. Finally, I want to see the volcanoes! #travel

5.title: My plans and predictions
5.brief: Write about your plans for next year and make two predictions about your country or your city.
5.briefEs: Escribe sobre tus planes del próximo año y haz dos predicciones sobre tu país o ciudad.
criteria: Three plans with “be going to”.
Two predictions with “will” or “won’t”.
Use “be likely to” once.
5.model: Next year is going to be very important for me. I'm going to finish my degree in June, and I'm going to look for a job in a tech company. I'm also going to take an English exam. About my city, I think the new metro line will be ready, so traffic won't be so bad. Prices are likely to go up, unfortunately. I think more tourists will come to Bogotá because it's becoming very popular.

5.title: Advice before an exam
5.brief: A friend has an important exam next week. Write an email with advice using modals of necessity and suggestion.
5.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo con consejos antes de un examen usando modales de necesidad y sugerencia.
criteria: Use must, have to, should and had better.
One negative: don’t have to or mustn’t.
Include “deadline”, “to postpone” or “to warn”.
5.model:
Hi Toño,

Your exam is next Tuesday, right? Here's my advice. You have to sleep well the night before — no parties! You should review your notes every day this week. You'd better start today because you mustn't leave everything for Monday. You don't have to study ten hours: two hours a day is enough. And I warn you, don't postpone the registration: the deadline is Friday!

Good luck!
Vale

5.title: Team plan for an event
5.brief: You are in charge of a small event at work or school. Write an email to the team with the plan: who is going to do what, what will happen and what is necessary.
5.briefEs: Escribe un correo al equipo con el plan de un evento: quién hará qué y qué es necesario.
criteria: Use “be going to” for decisions already made.
Use “will” for an offer or promise (I’ll send…).
Two modals of necessity (need to, have to, must).
5.model:
Hi team,

I'm in charge of the end-of-year event, so here's the plan. Andrés is going to book the room and Lina is going to order the food. The event is going to start at 6 p.m. We have to finish the decoration by 5:00, and everybody needs to bring one thing for the raffle. It's urgent: we must confirm the number of guests by Wednesday. I'll send the invitations tomorrow. We'd better have a backup plan in case it rains.

Thanks!
Daniela

5.title: Plans for Saturday
5.brief: Two friends talk about their weekend. Write a short chat with plans, an offer and a prediction.
5.briefEs: Dos amigos hablan de su fin de semana. Escribe un chat corto con planes, una oferta y una predicción.
criteria: Two plans with “be going to” or the present continuous.
One offer with “I’ll…” and one prediction with “will”.
End with a suggestion (Let’s…).
5.model:
What are you going to do on Saturday?
I'm going to visit my grandma. What about you?
I'm meeting Ana at the park. Do you want to come?
Sure, I'll bring some sandwiches.
Great! I think it will be sunny.
Let's meet at ten.

5.title: Study room rules
5.brief: Write a notice with the rules of the school study room. Say what people have to do, mustn't do and don't have to do.
5.briefEs: Escribe un aviso con las normas de la sala de estudio: qué deben hacer, qué no deben y qué no es obligatorio.
criteria: One obligation (have to / must) and one prohibition (mustn’t).
One “don’t have to” for something optional.
One piece of advice with “should” or “had better”.
5.model:
STUDY ROOM RULES

Welcome to the school study room. You have to sign the list at the door. You must keep your phone in your bag. You mustn't eat in the room, but you can drink water. You don't have to be silent in the corridor, but you should speak quietly. You need to leave the room by six. If you arrive late, you'd better tell the librarian. Thank you!

5.title: How to start running
5.brief: A friend wrote: “I want to start running. Any advice?” Reply with advice.
5.briefEs: Un amigo escribió: “Quiero empezar a correr. ¿Algún consejo?”. Respóndele con consejos.
criteria: Three pieces of advice with should, ought to, could or had better.
One “don’t have to” and one “had better not”.
Start with a greeting and finish with encouragement.
5.model:
Hi Jorge!

Great idea! My advice: you should start slowly, with ten minutes a day. You don't have to run fast at the beginning. You ought to buy good shoes, because bad shoes can hurt your feet. You'd better not run after a big meal. Also, you could ask a friend to run with you. I think you'll love it! Good luck!

5.title: Postponing the party
5.brief: Your party is not possible on the planned day. Write a message to your friends and give the new date.
5.briefEs: Tu fiesta no puede hacerse el día previsto. Escribe un mensaje a tus amigos con la nueva fecha.
criteria: Use “going to” for a forecast and “will” for an offer or promise.
Use “have to” or “need to” and the word “postpone”.
Give the new date and one request.
5.model:
Hi everyone,

I'm sorry, but we have to postpone the party. The forecast says it's going to rain on Saturday. The new date is next Saturday at seven. I'll send a new invitation today. Please tell me if you can't come, because we need to order enough food. I'm about to call the restaurant, and I will ask for a bigger table. Thanks for understanding!

Paula

5.title: Arriving at my host family
5.brief: You are going to stay with a host family in England. Write an email about your arrival plans.
5.briefEs: Vas a alojarte con una familia en Inglaterra. Escribe un correo sobre tus planes de llegada.
criteria: Two plans with “be going to” or the present continuous.
One offer or promise with “I’ll”.
One “have to”, one “must” and one “had better”.
5.model:
Dear Mrs Brown,

Thank you for your last message. My flight is arriving at Heathrow at nine on Sunday morning. I'm going to take the train to your town, and I'll call you from the station. I have to show my passport at the airport, so I must not forget it! I'm going to bring a small present from Colombia. What should I bring for the family? I'd better buy a warm coat, because it will be cold. See you soon!

Yours sincerely,
Santiago

5.title: Will robots take our jobs?
5.brief: Give your opinion about robots and jobs in the future. Use predictions and advice.
5.briefEs: Da tu opinión sobre los robots y el trabajo en el futuro, con predicciones y consejos.
criteria: Three predictions with will or won’t.
One “be likely to” and one “should” or “had better”.
A clear opinion at the start.
5.model: In my opinion, robots will do many jobs in the future. Factories are likely to use more machines, and shops will probably use robots too. Some people will lose their jobs, but new jobs will appear. I think teachers and doctors won't change, because people need people. We should learn new skills now. We had better study technology, or we might have problems. In my view, the future is going to be exciting.

6.title: Notes for the house-sitter
6.brief: Your friend is staying at your house while you are away. Write a note asking him or her to do several things with two-part verbs.
6.briefEs: Escribe una nota para la persona que cuida tu casa pidiéndole cosas con verbos de dos partes.
criteria: Five two-part verbs (turn off, pick up, put away, look after, fill in).
Correct position of the pronoun: turn it off, not turn off it.
Use “Could you…?” or “Would you mind…?” at least twice.
6.model: Hi Simón, thanks for looking after my house! Here are a few things. Could you water the plants every two days? Please feed the cat and look after her — she's very shy. Would you mind picking up my letters? Just put them on my desk. When you leave, please turn off the lights and turn them off in the garden too. Could you put away the dishes after you use them? If the gas man comes, please fill in the form for me. Thanks a million!

6.title: Replying to a request
6.brief: A colleague sent you three requests. Write a reply accepting two and refusing one politely.
6.briefEs: Responde a un colega aceptando dos de sus peticiones y rechazando una con cortesía.
criteria: Use “I’ll…” to accept requests.
Use “I’m afraid…” to refuse politely, with a reason.
Two expressions: right away, sort out, get back to you.
6.model:
Hi Claudia,

No problem, I'll send you the report right away. I'll also call the client and sort out the problem with the invoice. I'm afraid I can't go to the meeting on Friday because I have a doctor's appointment. Could you take notes for me? I'll get back to you on Monday with my comments.

Best,
Ricardo

6.title: A favour from a teacher
6.brief: Write an email to a teacher asking for two favours (e.g. more time for homework, a letter of recommendation). Be polite.
6.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un profesor pidiendo dos favores con mucha cortesía.
criteria: Use “Would you mind + -ing…?” once.
Use “Could you possibly…?” or “Would it be OK if…?”.
Use “to hand in” and “favour”.
6.model:
Dear Ms. Vargas,

I'm writing to ask you a favour. I was sick last week, so I couldn't finish my essay. Would you mind giving me two more days? I can hand it in on Thursday. Also, I am applying for a scholarship. Could you possibly write a short letter of recommendation for me? I understand if you are busy.

Thank you very much for your help.

Best regards,
Juan Camilo Ortiz

6.title: Sharing a study room
6.brief: Two students share a study room. Write a short chat with polite requests and answers.
6.briefEs: Dos estudiantes comparten una sala de estudio. Escribe un chat corto con peticiones corteses y respuestas.
criteria: One request with “Could you…?” and one with “Would you mind if I…?”.
Three two-part verbs with the pronoun in the right place (turn it off).
Answer with “Not at all” or “Of course”.
6.model:
Could you turn the music down, please?
Sorry! I'll turn it off right away.
Thanks. Would you mind if I opened the window?
Not at all. Could you pick up my notebook from the floor?
Of course. I'll put it away on your desk.
Thanks a lot!

6.title: Reminders for the school trip
6.brief: Write reminders for students before a school trip. Use two-part verbs.
6.briefEs: Escribe recordatorios para los estudiantes antes de una excursión, usando verbos de dos partes.
criteria: Five two-part verbs (hand in, fill in, pick up, turn off, put away, look after, sort out).
One pronoun between verb and particle (fill it in).
“Please” once and a closing offer with “I’ll…”.
6.model:
REMINDERS FOR FRIDAY'S TRIP

Please hand in the permission form by Wednesday. Fill it in with a black pen, and ask your parents to sign it. Pick up your bus ticket from the office at eight. Turn off your phone when the guide is talking. Look after your bag, because the museum is very crowded. Put away your lunch before you enter the rooms. If you have a problem, ask me and I'll sort it out right away.

6.title: A parcel for me
6.brief: A parcel is waiting for you at the post office. Write a message to a flatmate asking for a favour.
6.briefEs: Hay un paquete para ti en el correo. Escribe un mensaje a tu compañero de piso pidiéndole un favor.
criteria: “Would you mind + -ing” once and “Could you…?” once.
Use “I’m afraid” to explain why you can’t do it, with a reason.
Two two-part verbs (pick up, fill in).
6.model:
Hi Rafa,

Could you do me a favour? A parcel for me is at the post office near the station. Would you mind picking it up after work? You have to show your ID, and the staff will ask you to fill in a form. I'm afraid I can't go myself because I'm at the dentist until six. I'll pay you for the bus ticket. Could you text me when you have it? Thanks a million!

Juliana

6.title: Great service at a hostel
6.brief: Write a review of a hostel in Valparaíso where the staff helped you a lot.
6.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de un hostal en Valparaíso donde el personal te ayudó mucho.
criteria: Four two-part verbs in the past (picked up, sorted out, looked after, put away…).
One pronoun placed correctly (picked me up).
Use “right away” and mention one drawback.
6.model: The staff here are fantastic. They picked me up at the bus station at midnight, and they carried my bags upstairs. When I arrived, they helped me fill in the form and sorted out a problem with my room right away. In the morning, someone looked after the breakfast room and put away the dishes. The only drawback is the noise at night, so bring earplugs. I'll definitely come back!

6.title: Moving day
6.brief: Write a diary entry about the day you moved into a new flat.
6.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario sobre el día en que te mudaste a un apartamento nuevo.
criteria: Four two-part verbs.
Two pronouns placed correctly (sorted it out, hand it in).
Use “First” and “Then” to order the events.
6.model:
Saturday, 8 June

We moved into our new flat today. First, my brother picked up the van, and we put the boxes in it. At the new flat, I turned on the lights and looked after the plants. Then we put away the kitchen things. I couldn't open the door, but my dad sorted it out. I'm exhausted, but I'm happy! I will fill in the form for the internet tomorrow, and I'll hand it in on Monday.

6.title: Can friends ask too many favours?
6.brief: Give your opinion about asking friends for favours. Include a real example.
6.briefEs: Da tu opinión sobre pedir favores a los amigos e incluye un ejemplo real.
criteria: Use “do someone a favour” and “I’m afraid” once each.
One example with a two-part verb (hand in).
End with a clear opinion (In my opinion…).
6.model: I think it is fine to ask friends for a favour sometimes. A good friend will do you a favour, and you will do the same for them. However, it is not OK to ask for help all the time. Last month, a classmate asked me to hand in his homework three times, and I said no the third time. I'm afraid I can't help every day. In my opinion, a favour should be small, and you should always say thank you.

7.title: My favourite gadget
7.brief: Describe a device you use every day. Say what it is used for and why it comes in handy.
7.briefEs: Describe un aparato que usas a diario: para qué sirve y por qué te resulta útil.
criteria: Use “is used for + -ing” and “is used to + verb”.
Use “in order to” once.
Include “device”, “tool” or “to come in handy”.
7.model: My favourite device is my e-reader. It's used for reading books, but I also use it to read articles from the internet. It's very light, so it comes in handy when I travel. I use it every night in order to relax before I sleep. It's also useful for learning English because I can touch a word to see the meaning. The battery lasts for weeks. It wasn't cheap, but it was worth every peso!

7.title: How to survive your first day
7.brief: Write tips for a new student or worker on their first day. Use imperatives and infinitives to give suggestions.
7.briefEs: Escribe consejos para el primer día de un estudiante o trabajador nuevo con imperativos e infinitivos.
criteria: Four imperatives (Arrive…, Don’t forget…).
Two suggestions with “Try to…” or “Remember to…”.
Use “to make sure” and “to avoid”.
7.model: Your first day can be stressful, so here are some tips. Arrive ten minutes early to avoid stress. Make sure you have your ID and a notebook. Don't forget to smile and introduce yourself. Try to remember people's names: write them down if necessary. Ask questions — it's normal not to know everything. Remember to bring your lunch, because the cafeteria is expensive. Finally, don't worry too much. Everyone was new once!

7.title: An instruction message
7.brief: Your grandmother has a new smartphone. Write a message explaining how to make a video call.
7.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a tu abuela explicándole cómo hacer una videollamada en su celular nuevo.
criteria: Use imperatives in the correct order with sequence words.
Use “to keep + -ing” once.
Explain the purpose of one step with “to” or “in order to”.
7.model: Hi Grandma! To make a video call, follow these steps. First, open the green app with the phone. Then find my name and touch it. After that, press the small camera icon to start the video. Keep holding the phone in front of your face so I can see you! To end the call, press the red button. Don't worry if it doesn't work the first time. Keep trying, and call me if you need help. Love you!

7.title: Wireless earphones: worth buying?
7.brief: Write a review of a device you bought. Say what it is used for and if it is worth buying.
7.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de un aparato que compraste: para qué se usa y si vale la pena.
criteria: Use “in order to” once and “used for + -ing” once.
Use “worth + -ing” and “come in handy”.
One warning with “Avoid + -ing”.
7.model: I bought these earphones three months ago in order to listen to music on the bus. They are also used for making calls, and the sound is clear. I use them to study, and they come in handy in noisy places. Avoid running with them because they fall out. The battery lasts for six hours, which is enough for me. They cost forty pounds, and I think they are worth buying. Four stars!

7.title: Safety in the science lab
7.brief: Write a safety notice for a school science lab using imperatives and purpose.
7.briefEs: Escribe un aviso de seguridad para el laboratorio de ciencias usando imperativos y finalidad.
criteria: Four imperatives, one of them negative.
One purpose clause with “in order to” and one with “to”.
Use “make sure”, “avoid” and “is for + -ing” once each.
7.model:
SAFETY IN THE SCIENCE LAB

Wear your goggles in order to protect your eyes. Tie back long hair to avoid accidents. Don't eat or drink in the lab. Make sure you read the instructions before you start. Use the small tool to move hot glass. Never run, and keep working quietly. If something breaks, tell the teacher at once. The red button is for stopping the gas in an emergency.

7.title: What's this tool for?
7.brief: You are in a shop. Write a short conversation to ask what a tool is for and buy it.
7.briefEs: Estás en una tienda. Escribe una conversación corta para preguntar para qué sirve una herramienta y comprarla.
criteria: Ask “What’s … for?” and answer with “It’s used for + -ing”.
One purpose with “to + verb”.
One instruction with “Make sure…”.
7.model:
What's this tool for?
It's used for cutting paper. Do you want one?
Yes, please. I need it to make cards.
Here you are. Make sure you keep it away from children.
Thanks. How much is it?
It's five pounds.

7.title: Borrowing a ladder
7.brief: Write an email to a neighbour to borrow a tool. Explain why you need it.
7.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un vecino para pedirle una herramienta prestada y explicar para qué la necesitas.
criteria: Purpose with “in order to” and with “to + verb”.
Use “avoid + -ing” once.
Greeting, polite request and closing.
7.model:
Hi Mr Santos,

I hope you are well. I'm writing to ask for a favour. I'd like to borrow your ladder in order to paint my bedroom. The ceiling is too high for me to reach. I will use it for two hours on Saturday, and I'll bring it back in the evening. Please tell me if you need it, because I want to avoid causing a problem. I can bring you a cake in return!

Best wishes,
Elena

7.title: Is social media worth it?
7.brief: Give your opinion about social media. Say what you use it for and what you avoid.
7.briefEs: Da tu opinión sobre las redes sociales: para qué las usas y qué evitas.
criteria: Use “worth + -ing” and “the point of + -ing”.
Use “avoid + -ing” and a purpose with “to + verb”.
Use “tool” and “make sure”.
7.model: I think social media is worth using, but only for a short time. I use my phone to talk to friends and to see their photos. I avoid checking it at night, and I keep my phone away from my bed. What's the point of scrolling for hours? In my opinion, an app is a tool, and it should come in handy, not waste our time. Make sure you have time for real life too.

7.title: Directions to my house
7.brief: A friend is coming to your house by bus. Write the directions step by step.
7.briefEs: Un amigo irá a tu casa en bus. Escribe las indicaciones paso a paso.
criteria: Five imperatives in order, one negative (Don’t…).
One purpose with “in order to” and one with “to avoid”.
Use “keep + -ing”.
7.model: Take the number nine bus from the station in order to get to my street. Get off at the second stop, next to the big bakery. Walk straight and turn left at the traffic lights. Don't take the small road on the right, because it is too dark at night. Cross the park to avoid the hill. My house is the green one with a blue door. Call me if you get lost, and keep walking until you see it!

8.title: A turning point in my life
8.brief: Write about a moment that changed your life. Use relative clauses with “when” and time clauses with when, after and before.
8.briefEs: Escribe sobre un momento que cambió tu vida usando cláusulas con when, after y before.
criteria: One relative clause of time (the day when…, the year when…).
Two clauses with after / before / as soon as.
Use “turning point”, “to realise” or “eventually”.
8.model: 2020 was the year when everything changed for me. Before the pandemic started, I worked in a call centre and I was unhappy. When the offices closed, I had a lot of time at home. I started to bake bread while I was waiting for news. After my neighbours tried my bread, they asked me to sell it. That was the turning point. As soon as I realised I could earn money, I made a website. Eventually, I opened my own bakery.

8.title: A day of my life, in order
8.brief: Write a diary entry about a busy day. Connect the events with when, after, before, as soon as and while.
8.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario de un día ocupado conectando eventos con when, after, before, while.
criteria: Four time connectors (when, after, before, as soon as, while, until).
Use a comma when the time clause comes first.
Use “meanwhile” or “in the meantime”.
8.model: What a day! As soon as I woke up, I checked my emails. Before I had breakfast, my boss called me. While I was talking to him, the coffee burned! After I left home, I realised I didn't have my keys. I waited for my roommate until 11:00. Meanwhile, I answered messages on my phone. When I finally arrived at the office, the meeting was over. Tomorrow will be better!

8.title: Graduation memories
8.brief: Write an email to an old classmate remembering your graduation day. Describe what happened at different moments.
8.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un excompañero recordando el día de su graduación.
criteria: Use “the day when” or “the moment when”.
Two time clauses with after / by the time / until.
Use “to graduate” and one more word from the unit.
8.model:
Hi Luisa,

Do you remember the day when we graduated? I was looking at the photos today. Before the ceremony started, we were so nervous! By the time my name was called, my hands were shaking. After we received our diplomas, we threw our hats in the air. Then we danced until the sun came up. That was the moment when I realised we were adults. I miss you!

Hugs,
Fer

8.title: Plans for a study session
8.brief: Write a message to a friend with the plan for tomorrow's study session. Order the plan with time clauses.
8.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un amigo con el plan de mañana para estudiar, ordenándolo con cláusulas de tiempo.
criteria: Four future time clauses with as soon as, when, before, after, while or until.
No “will” inside the time clause.
A comma after each time clause that opens the sentence.
8.model:
Hi Gaby,

I'll call you as soon as I finish work tomorrow. When I get home, I'll have dinner and then I'll open the notes. Before you start the exercises, please read the text. I'll wait until you answer, and then we can decide the plan. After we finish the first part, we'll take a break. While you're making coffee, I'll check the answers. We won't stop until we finish everything!

Bea

8.title: Open day at our school
8.brief: Write an announcement for the school open day. Say what happens and when.
8.briefEs: Escribe un anuncio para el día de puertas abiertas del colegio: qué pasa y cuándo.
criteria: One relative clause of time (the day when…).
Three time clauses with when, before, while, after or until.
Present simple (not “will”) inside the time clauses.
8.model:
WELCOME TO OUR OPEN DAY

The day when new students visit our school is Saturday 11 May. When you arrive, please sign in at the main desk. Before the tour starts, you can have a free drink in the café. While the guides show you the classrooms, parents can talk to the director. After the tour finishes, we will give you a small present. Stay with your group until the activities end. We hope to see you soon!

8.title: Why are you late?
8.brief: A friend asks why you were late. Write a short conversation that explains the events in order.
8.briefEs: Un amigo te pregunta por qué llegaste tarde. Escribe una conversación corta que explique los hechos en orden.
criteria: Two past time clauses with when, until or by the time.
One question “What happened…?”.
Use “realised” and one past continuous.
8.model:
Why are you late?
When I was waiting for the bus, I realised I had no money.
So what did you do?
I walked until I found a cash machine.
What happened after that?
By the time I arrived, the class was over.

8.title: Exam day plan
8.brief: Write a plan for the day of an exam. Say what to do before, during and after it.
8.briefEs: Escribe un plan para el día de un examen: qué hacer antes, durante y después.
criteria: Five time clauses with different conjunctions (before, when, while, after, until, as soon as).
Imperatives in the main clause.
A comma when the time clause comes first.
8.model: Before you leave home, check your bag. Take your ID and two pens. When you arrive at school, find your room and sit down. While you're waiting for the teacher, don't talk about the answers. After the teacher gives you the paper, read all the questions first. Don't write anything until you understand the task. As soon as you finish, check your work. When time is up, hand in your paper and relax.

8.title: A festival night
8.brief: Write a review of a music festival you went to in Guadalajara. Include a price in pesos.
8.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de un festival de música al que fuiste en Guadalajara. Incluye un precio en pesos.
criteria: One relative clause of time (the moment when…).
Three time clauses with while, before, after or until.
Use “eventually” and a price in pesos.
8.model: Last Saturday I went to the music festival in Guadalajara. The moment when the main band appeared at ten was the best. While they were playing, everyone sang and danced. Before the concert started, we waited in a long queue for an hour. After we entered, the sound was excellent. The bad part was the food: we paid 150 pesos for a small burger. I stayed until the end, and eventually I got home at three. Four stars!

8.title: A letter to myself
8.brief: Write a letter to yourself to read in ten years. Say what you will do and when.
8.briefEs: Escribe una carta a ti mismo para leer dentro de diez años: qué harás y cuándo.
criteria: One relative clause of time (the day when…).
Three future time clauses (When, Until, As soon as, By the time) in the present simple.
A greeting and a closing.
8.model:
Dear Future Me,

In ten years, you will read this letter. By the time you open it, you will probably live in a different city. I hope you remember the day when I wrote this letter. When I finish my degree, I'll look for a job abroad. Until I find one, I'll keep studying English every day. As soon as I save enough money, I'll travel to Japan. I hope you are happy!

Yours,
Me, aged 17

9.title: My town: past, present and future
9.brief: Write a short article for a school magazine about how your town has changed and how it will be in twenty years.
9.briefEs: Escribe un artículo corto sobre cómo ha cambiado tu ciudad y cómo será en veinte años.
criteria: Use a past form (used to, was), a present form (nowadays) and a future form (will).
Include “trend” or “gradually”.
One first conditional sentence.
9.model: Zipaquirá has changed a lot. Thirty years ago, it used to be a quiet town with only a few shops. People used to travel to Bogotá by train. Nowadays, it is a popular tourist destination and there are hotels and restaurants everywhere. The population is gradually growing. In twenty years, I think it will be part of Bogotá. If the city builds a train line, people will live here and work in the capital. Unless we protect the parks, there won't be any green areas left.

9.title: If you visit my city…
9.brief: A friend is planning to visit your city. Write an email giving advice with first conditional sentences.
9.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo que viene de visita con consejos usando el primer condicional.
criteria: Four first conditional sentences (If + present, will + verb).
Use “unless” and “in case” once each.
Use a comma when the if-clause comes first.
9.model:
Hi Tom,

I'm so happy you're coming to Medellín! If you arrive on a Friday, we'll go to a salsa class together. If you like coffee, I'll take you to a farm near the city. Bring an umbrella in case it rains — it usually rains in the afternoon. Unless you want to get lost, download the metro map. If you get tired, we'll take a cable car to see the view. You'll love it!

See you soon,
Andrés

9.title: What will happen if…?
9.brief: Choose a problem (traffic, pollution, too much screen time). Write about the consequences if people don't change.
9.briefEs: Elige un problema (tráfico, contaminación, pantallas) y escribe sus consecuencias si la gente no cambia.
criteria: Three first conditional sentences about consequences.
Use “as long as” once.
Use “consequence” and “to improve”.
9.model: Screen time is a big problem for children nowadays. If kids spend six hours a day on screens, they won't sleep well. If they don't play outside, they will have health problems. Another consequence is that they won't talk to their families. But the situation can improve. As long as parents set rules, children will use phones in a healthy way. If schools organise more sports, kids will be more active. We need to act now.

9.title: What will you do if it rains?
9.brief: Two friends plan the weekend. Write a short conversation with conditions and consequences.
9.briefEs: Dos amigos planean el fin de semana. Escribe una conversación corta con condiciones y consecuencias.
criteria: Two first conditional sentences or questions (If + present, will + verb).
Use “unless”, “as long as” and “in case” once each.
Short lines, as in a natural chat.
9.model:
What will you do if it rains on Saturday?
If it rains, I'll stay at home.
We could go to the cinema unless you have a better idea.
I'll come as long as the film isn't too long.
I'll check the times in case it's full.

9.title: Shopping: then and now
9.brief: Write a post about how shopping has changed and what may happen next.
9.briefEs: Escribe una publicación sobre cómo han cambiado las compras y qué puede pasar después.
criteria: One contrast with “used to” and one with “nowadays”.
Two first conditional sentences.
Use “trend” or “gradually” and “expect”.
9.model: Shopping has changed a lot! Back then, people used to go to the market every day. Nowadays, many people order food on their phones, and a delivery arrives in thirty minutes. This trend is gradually growing. If it continues, small shops will close. I expect more people to buy online in the future. But if we support local shops, they will stay open. What do you prefer? #thenandnow

9.title: Packing for a camping trip
9.brief: Write a message to a friend with advice for a camping trip.
9.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un amigo con consejos para una excursión de camping.
criteria: Use “in case”, “unless” and “as long as” once each.
Two sentences with “If” + present simple and “will”.
A greeting and a closing.
9.model:
Hi Sam,

Here is my advice for the camping trip. Take a raincoat in case it rains. If the weather is good, we'll swim in the river. We won't light a fire unless the park allows it. You can bring your guitar as long as it isn't too heavy. If you get cold at night, you'll need a warm sleeping bag. Don't forget some snacks, because we'll end up hungry! See you on Friday.

Lola

9.title: My exam promises
9.brief: Write a diary entry with promises to yourself before an exam. Say what will happen if you do or don't do things.
9.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario con promesas para ti antes de un examen: qué pasará si haces o no ciertas cosas.
criteria: Two “if” sentences and one “unless” sentence (first conditional).
Use “nowadays” or “gradually” once.
End with a promise to yourself.
9.model:
Sunday, 3 November

The exam is in two weeks, and I'm worried. If I study every day, I will pass. Unless I stop checking my phone, I won't finish the book. I'll go out with my friends as long as I finish my homework first. I'll take my notes to the library in case my room is too noisy. Nowadays, I don't study enough, but I'm going to change. If I improve my English gradually, I will feel more confident.

9.title: Join our bike club
9.brief: Write an advertisement for a bike club. Say what happens if people join and how the club has changed.
9.briefEs: Escribe un anuncio para un club de ciclismo: qué pasa si te unes y cómo ha cambiado el club.
criteria: Two first conditionals (If + present, will).
One contrast “Back then… nowadays”.
Use “expect” or “trend”.
9.model:
JOIN OUR BIKE CLUB

If you join this month, you'll get a free helmet. You can come to any ride as long as you wear it. We start at eight, and we won't wait unless you call us. Bring water in case it's hot. If it rains, we'll meet at the café instead. Back then, our club had only five members; nowadays we have fifty, and we expect more soon. If you like cycling, you'll love us. Don't wait!

9.title: Fire drill instructions
9.brief: Write instructions for a school fire drill using conditions and imperatives.
9.briefEs: Escribe instrucciones para un simulacro de incendio en el colegio usando condiciones e imperativos.
criteria: Three “if” sentences with the present simple in the if-clause.
Use “unless” once and “as long as” once.
Imperatives for at least three steps.
9.model: If the alarm rings, stop your work and leave the room. Don't take your bags unless they are next to the door. Walk to the football field and wait for your teacher. If you stay calm, everyone will get out safely. If the corridor is full of smoke, stay low and use the other stairs. We will practise this plan twice a year in case there is a real emergency. As long as you follow these steps, you will be safe.

10.title: Things I love and hate
10.brief: Write about activities you enjoy and activities you can't stand. Explain why.
10.briefEs: Escribe sobre actividades que disfrutas y que no soportas, y explica por qué.
criteria: Five verbs followed by gerunds (enjoy, can’t stand, don’t mind, prefer, be into).
Three clauses with “because” and one with “because of”.
Use “fed up with” or “bored / boring”.
10.model: I really enjoy cooking for my friends because it relaxes me. I'm also into hiking: I go every weekend because of the fresh air. I don't mind washing the dishes, but I can't stand ironing clothes because it's so boring. I prefer listening to podcasts to watching TV. I'm fed up with waiting for the bus every morning, so I'm thinking of buying a bike. What about you?

10.title: Answer a friend's profile
10.brief: Reply to this post: “I love dancing. I don't like getting up early. I can't stand rainy days.” Agree or disagree with short responses and give reasons.
10.briefEs: Responde a un post diciendo si coincides o no con respuestas cortas y razones.
criteria: Short responses: So do I. / Neither do I. / I do. / I don’t.
Gerunds after like / love / can’t stand.
Two reasons with “because”.
10.model: Hi! I read your post. You love dancing? So do I! I take salsa classes because it's great exercise. You don't like getting up early? Neither do I. I'm a night person, so mornings are terrible for me. But I don't agree about rainy days. I love them because I can stay home, read and drink hot chocolate. Maybe we can go dancing one day — but not in the morning!

10.title: A review of a hobby class
10.brief: Write a review of a class or course you took (dance, cooking, yoga). Say what you enjoyed and didn't enjoy and why.
10.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una clase que tomaste: lo que disfrutaste, lo que no y por qué.
criteria: Four gerunds as objects (I enjoyed learning…).
Use “because” and “because of” correctly.
Use “to be worth it” and one -ed / -ing adjective pair.
10.model: I took a pottery class for six weeks at the community centre. I really enjoyed working with my hands because it was relaxing. I loved making my own cups. The teacher was patient and the classes were never boring. I didn't enjoy cleaning the room at the end, and I was sometimes bored because of the long explanations. But I don't mind getting dirty, so I had fun. The course was cheap and it was definitely worth it. I recommend it!

10.title: Planning a film night
10.brief: Two friends plan a film night. Write a short chat with likes, dislikes and short responses.
10.briefEs: Dos amigos planean una noche de cine. Escribe un chat corto con gustos, disgustos y respuestas cortas.
criteria: One “So do I” and one “Neither can I” with the matching auxiliary.
Three gerunds after love, enjoy, can’t stand, prefer or don’t mind.
End with a plan using “Let’s…”.
10.model:
I love watching horror films.
So do I! I enjoy being scared.
I can't stand waiting in queues at the cinema.
Neither can I. I prefer watching films at home.
I don't mind cooking snacks.
Great! Let's start at eight.

10.title: Host family form
10.brief: Complete a form for a host family. Write full sentences about your habits and preferences.
10.briefEs: Completa un formulario para una familia anfitriona con oraciones completas sobre tus hábitos y preferencias.
criteria: Five gerunds after enjoy, don’t mind, can’t stand, prefer, love or be into.
Two reasons with “because” and two with “because of”.
Use “fed up with”.
10.model: I enjoy cooking, so I don't mind helping in the kitchen. I can't stand loud music at night because I need sleep. I prefer eating at home to eating out because of the price. I'm into football, and I love playing with other students. I'm also fed up with cold showers, so a warm bathroom is important. I don't mind sharing a room because I'm sociable. Because of my English course, I will be at home only in the evenings.

10.title: Cats or dogs?
10.brief: Write your opinion: do you prefer cats or dogs? Give reasons.
10.briefEs: Escribe tu opinión: ¿prefieres gatos o perros? Da razones.
criteria: Use “prefer … to …” and “because”.
Two gerunds after enjoy, don’t mind or can’t stand.
Use “because of” once and “worth it” once.
10.model: I prefer dogs to cats because they are more friendly. I enjoy walking my dog every morning, and I don't mind cleaning up after him. Cats are nice, but I can't stand their hair on my clothes. Many people prefer cats because of their independence, and I understand that. However, I think dogs are more fun. Having a dog is worth it because of the love you get. What about you?

10.title: A gift for Marco
10.brief: Write a message to a friend to ask for help choosing a present for someone. Describe what he likes and dislikes.
10.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a una amiga pidiendo ayuda para elegir un regalo: cuenta qué le gusta y qué no.
criteria: Four verbs followed by a gerund (enjoys, can’t stand, doesn’t mind, prefers … to…).
One “because of” and one “so”.
Ask a question and use “worth”.
10.model:
Hi Ana,

I need help with a present for Marco. He's into photography and he enjoys taking photos of old buildings. He can't stand wearing formal clothes, so a shirt isn't a good idea. He doesn't mind reading, but he prefers watching documentaries to reading books. I don't want to spend too much money because of my new phone. What do you think? Maybe a small camera bag is worth buying. Thanks!

Leo

10.title: Join the photo club
10.brief: Write an advertisement for a school club. Say what members enjoy and prefer.
10.briefEs: Escribe un anuncio para un club del colegio: qué disfrutan y prefieren los miembros.
criteria: Five gerund uses after enjoy, don’t mind, love, prefer or be into.
Two reasons with “because”.
A title with a question and an invitation to join.
10.model:
ARE YOU INTO PHOTOGRAPHY?

Our school photo club needs new members! Do you enjoy taking photos of people or nature? We don't mind beginners, because we love teaching new students. We prefer meeting on Thursdays to meeting at weekends, because most of us have football on Saturdays. You don't need a big camera: your phone is enough. Taking photos is more fun with friends, so come and share it with us. It's definitely worth trying!

10.title: A boring Sunday
10.brief: Write a diary entry about a boring Sunday. Say how you felt and why.
10.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario sobre un domingo aburrido: cómo te sentiste y por qué.
criteria: One boring / bored pair used correctly.
“Because of” once and “because” once.
Three gerunds after verbs such as don’t mind, prefer or be fed up with.
10.model:
Sunday, 24 March

Today was boring, and I'm bored of staying at home. Because of the rain, I couldn't go cycling. I don't mind reading, but I finished my book yesterday. My brother prefers playing video games to talking, so he didn't want to chat. I'm fed up with doing the same things every weekend. Next Sunday, I'm trying rock climbing with my cousin because I'm into new things. It sounds interesting, but I'm a bit scared.

11.title: A famous invention
11.brief: Write a short text about a famous invention or building. Say who invented or built it, when, and how it is used today.
11.briefEs: Escribe un texto informativo sobre un invento o edificio famoso con la voz pasiva.
criteria: Three passive sentences in the past with “by” (was invented by).
Two passive sentences in the present (is used, are made).
Correct past participles (built, made, written).
11.model: The telephone was invented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876. The first call was made to his assistant, Thomas Watson. At first, the telephone was used only by rich people and businesses. Later, millions of phones were produced in factories around the world. Today, mobile phones are used by almost everyone. They are made in many countries, and they are used for calls, messages, photos and much more. Old telephones are now shown in museums.

11.title: How coffee is produced
11.brief: Describe how a Colombian product (coffee, chocolate, panela, flowers) is produced. Use the passive in the present.
11.briefEs: Describe cómo se produce un producto colombiano usando la voz pasiva en presente.
criteria: Six passive verbs in the present simple (is grown, are picked…).
Use sequence words: first, then, after that, finally.
Include “to be based on”, “to deliver” or “to carry out”.
11.model: Colombian coffee is famous all over the world. First, the coffee plants are grown on farms in the mountains. Then the red cherries are picked by hand. After that, the beans are washed and dried in the sun. Next, the beans are sorted and quality tests are carried out. The coffee is packed in big bags and it is delivered to ports. Finally, it is sold in many countries. Most of it is exported to the USA.

11.title: News: a robbery in my street
11.brief: Write a short news report about something that happened (a robbery, a fire, an accident). Focus on the action using the passive.
11.briefEs: Escribe una noticia corta sobre un suceso enfocándote en la acción con la voz pasiva.
criteria: Four passive verbs in the past (was stolen, were damaged).
Use “by” only when the agent is important.
A short title and one active sentence for contrast.
11.model:
BANK ROBBED IN CHAPINERO
A small bank was robbed yesterday morning in Chapinero. About 20 million pesos were stolen. Two windows were damaged and one employee was hurt, but not seriously. The robbers were seen by a taxi driver, who called the police. The area was closed for three hours. Two men were arrested last night. The police are still looking for the money.

11.title: Library closed notice
11.brief: Write a notice for the school board explaining that the library is closed and what has been done. Use the passive.
11.briefEs: Escribe un aviso para el tablero explicando que la biblioteca está cerrada y qué se ha hecho. Usa la voz pasiva.
criteria: Four passives in the past or present (was damaged, are checked…).
One passive with “by” and one without an agent.
Use “allowed” or “required”.
11.model:
NOTICE: LIBRARY CLOSED

The school library was closed on Monday because the roof was damaged by the storm. Many books were moved to the gym, and the library floor is cleaned every day. The books are checked by our staff before they are returned to the shelves. Students are not allowed to enter the library until Friday. Homework is collected in the gym. Lost books are reported at the main office. Thank you for your patience.

11.title: A parcel delivered to the wrong address
11.brief: Write a formal email to a shop. Your parcel was delivered to the wrong address and it was damaged.
11.briefEs: Escribe un correo formal a una tienda: tu paquete fue entregado en una dirección equivocada y llegó dañado.
criteria: Four passive sentences in the past (was delivered, was damaged…).
One passive with “by” and an agent.
A formal greeting, a request (Could you please…?) and a closing.
11.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about my order of a phone case, number 4521. The parcel was delivered to the wrong address on Monday. It was damaged, and the box was opened. I was not told about the problem by your company. I was promised a delivery in two days, but nothing was explained to me. Could you please send me a new one? My address is 12 Station Road. Please reply to me soon.

Yours faithfully,
Harriet Cole

11.title: At the chocolate factory
11.brief: You visit a chocolate factory in Ecuador. Write a short conversation with the guide using passive questions.
11.briefEs: Visitas una fábrica de chocolate en Ecuador. Escribe una conversación corta con el guía usando preguntas en pasiva.
criteria: Three passive questions with is / was / are.
At least two passive answers with the correct participle (grown, built).
Use “allowed to” once.
11.model:
Is the chocolate made here?
Yes, it is. The cocoa is grown in Ecuador and then it's brought here.
When was the factory built?
It was built in 1990.
Are visitors allowed to taste it?
Yes, you are!

11.title: Who broke the window?
11.brief: Write a short story about a mystery at school. Use the passive to focus on the events.
11.briefEs: Escribe una historia corta sobre un misterio en el colegio usando la voz pasiva para centrarte en los hechos.
criteria: Five past passives with correct participles.
At least one passive with “by + agent” and others without an agent.
Events in order with a clear ending.
11.model: On Friday morning, the school was quiet. At nine o'clock, the teacher saw that a window in the science lab was broken. The glass was on the floor, and a football was found under a desk. The football was kept by Mr Reed until the end of the day. Many students were asked questions, but nobody was seen near the lab. In the end, the window was repaired by the caretaker, and the mystery was never solved.

11.title: Our old market
11.brief: Write a social media post about an old market in your town. Say what was done in the past and what is done today.
11.briefEs: Escribe una publicación sobre un mercado antiguo de tu ciudad: qué se hizo en el pasado y qué se hace hoy.
criteria: Three past passives (was built, was damaged, was repaired).
Three present passives (are sold, are made, is visited).
Use “by + agent” at least twice.
