11.model: This is the old market in my town. It was built in 1920 by local workers. The roof was damaged by a fire in 2005, but it was repaired in two years. Today, fresh fruit and cheese are sold here, and handmade bags are made by local women. The market is visited by hundreds of people on Saturdays. Photos aren't allowed inside the cheese shop, but they are allowed outside. Come and see it! #oldmarket

11.title: Should phones be allowed in class?
11.brief: Give your opinion about phones in class. Use the passive to describe the rules.
11.briefEs: Da tu opinión sobre los celulares en clase usando la pasiva para describir las normas.
criteria: Four present passives (are kept, are returned, are interrupted…).
One passive with “allowed” and one with “by + agent”.
Give your opinion with “In my opinion” and one reason with “because”.
11.model: In my school, phones are not allowed in class. They are kept in a box by the teacher, and they are returned at the end of the day. I think this rule is fair because lessons are often interrupted by notifications. However, phones can be used for learning, for example to look up words. In my opinion, phones should be allowed for short activities. If the rules are explained clearly, students will follow them.

12.title: When the lights went out
12.brief: Write a story about a time when something interrupted you (a blackout, a phone call, an earthquake). Use the past continuous and the simple past.
12.briefEs: Escribe una historia sobre una interrupción usando pasado continuo y pasado simple.
criteria: Three past continuous verbs for background actions.
Two interruptions with “when” + simple past.
Use “suddenly” or “just then” and one word from the unit.
12.model: It was a stormy night. I was studying for a test and my sister was watching a horror film. My parents were cooking dinner. Suddenly, the lights went out. My sister screamed! While we were looking for candles, someone knocked on the door. We were so scared. Just then, my dad opened the door and it was our neighbour, Don Jorge. He was carrying a big lamp. We all laughed and had dinner together by candlelight.

12.title: What I've been doing lately
12.brief: Write an email to a friend telling him or her what you have been doing lately. Use the present perfect continuous.
12.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo contándole qué has estado haciendo últimamente.
criteria: Four verbs in the present perfect continuous (have been working…).
Use “lately / recently” and “for / since”.
One sentence about how you feel (exhausted, excited).
12.model:
Hi Lina!

Sorry I haven't written. I've been working really hard lately. I've been helping my boss with a new project since January, so I'm exhausted. I've also been taking guitar lessons for two months. My neighbour hates it! And my brother has been staying with me because he's been looking for a flat. What have you been doing recently?

Hugs,
Ángela

12.title: A progress report
12.brief: Write a short report about a project you are still working on (a garden, a course, saving money). Say how long you have been doing it and what happened along the way.
12.briefEs: Escribe un informe corto sobre un proyecto en curso: desde cuándo lo haces y qué ha pasado.
criteria: Two present perfect continuous verbs with for / since.
One past continuous + simple past (I was planting when…).
Use “progress”, “to deal with” or “to keep an eye on”.
12.model:
Project: my vegetable garden
I have been growing vegetables on my balcony since March. I have been reading a lot about plants, and I have made good progress: I have tomatoes, lettuce and herbs now. Last month there was a problem. I was watering the plants when I saw small insects on the leaves. I dealt with them using a natural spray. Now I keep an eye on the plants every morning. I have been saving money because I don't buy vegetables any more!

12.title: An alibi
12.brief: A detective asks you what you were doing last night. Write a short conversation.
12.briefEs: Un detective te pregunta qué hacías anoche. Escribe una conversación corta.
criteria: Two past continuous sentences (was watching…).
One interruption with “Suddenly” + simple past.
A question “What were you doing…?” and a short answer (Yes, I was.).
12.model:
What were you doing at nine last night?
I was watching a film with my sister.
Were you at home all evening?
Yes, I was. Suddenly, the doorbell rang, and my sister went to the door.
Who was it?
It was a neighbour with a letter.

12.title: Sorry I missed your call
12.brief: A friend called you three times. Write a message to explain what you were doing and what you have been doing lately.
12.briefEs: Un amigo te llamó tres veces. Escribe un mensaje explicando qué hacías y qué has estado haciendo últimamente.
criteria: Two past continuous sentences and one interruption with “when” + simple past.
Two present perfect continuous sentences with all day, all week, for or since.
Use “exhausted” and a polite apology.
12.model:
Hi Dani,

Sorry I didn't answer your call! I was cycling to the gym when my phone rang, so I couldn't pick it up. Then I was talking to my trainer for an hour. While I was changing, I saw your three missed calls. I've been working all day, and I'm exhausted. Can I call you at eight? Happy birthday for tomorrow! I've been looking for a present all week.

Alex

12.title: Learning to skate
12.brief: Write a post about something you have been learning. Say how long and what happened one day.
12.briefEs: Escribe una publicación sobre algo que has estado aprendiendo: cuánto tiempo y qué pasó un día.
criteria: Four sentences in the present perfect continuous with for, since or lately.
One past continuous + simple past interruption (I was skating… when…).
Use “progress” or “keep an eye on”.
12.model: I've been learning to skate for three weeks, and I'm still falling a lot! I've been practising in the park every evening since March. Yesterday, I was skating down a small hill when a dog ran across the path. I fell, but nothing was broken. I've been keeping an eye on my balance, and I'm making progress. A friend has been helping me, and she says I'm improving. What have you been learning lately? #skating

12.title: Lost dog
12.brief: Your dog ran away in a park in Bogotá. Write a notice to find him.
12.briefEs: Tu perro se escapó en un parque de Bogotá. Escribe un aviso para encontrarlo.
criteria: One past continuous with an interruption (I was walking… when…).
Two present perfect continuous sentences with all day or since.
A description of the dog and a contact number.
12.model:
LOST DOG: PLEASE HELP

Our dog, Milo, ran away yesterday afternoon. I was walking in Simón Bolívar Park when he heard a loud noise. Suddenly, he pulled the lead and ran towards the lake. I have been looking for him all day, and my family has been searching since last night. He is small and brown, and he was wearing a red collar. If you saw him, please call me on 300 555 0147. We are exhausted and very worried.

12.title: Questions for a marathon runner
12.brief: You are going to interview a marathon runner. Write five questions.
12.briefEs: Vas a entrevistar a un corredor de maratón. Escribe cinco preguntas.
criteria: Four questions in the present perfect continuous (with for, since or lately).
One past continuous + “when” question.
Use “How long…?” once.
12.model:
How long have you been training for marathons?
What were you doing when you decided to run your first race?
Have you been following a special diet lately?
How have you been preparing for the next race?
What have you been listening to while you run?

12.title: A series I can't stop watching
12.brief: Write a review of a TV series you have been watching.
12.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de una serie de televisión que has estado viendo.
criteria: Two present perfect continuous sentences with for or since.
One interruption (was studying… when…).
Your opinion and a star rating.
12.model: I've been watching this science-fiction series for two weeks, and I can't stop! It's about a group of students who find a secret door at school. I was studying for an exam when my friend recommended it, and I started the first episode that night. I've been staying up late since then, so I'm a bit tired. The acting is great, and the story is full of surprises. I give it four stars.

13.title: A disappointing trip
13.brief: Write an email about a trip that was not as good as you expected. Use participle adjectives (-ing and -ed).
13.briefEs: Escribe un correo sobre un viaje decepcionante usando adjetivos terminados en -ing y -ed.
criteria: Three pairs or forms of -ing / -ed adjectives used correctly.
One relative clause with “who” and one with “which / that”.
Include “disappointing”, “exhausting” or “annoying”.
13.model:
Hi Paula,

I'm back from San Andrés and, honestly, the trip was disappointing. The flight was delayed for six hours, which was really annoying. When we arrived, we were exhausted. The hotel that we booked was far from the beach. The tour guide, who was very friendly, tried to help, but the weather was terrible: it rained every day! I was bored most of the time. The only fascinating thing was the colour of the sea.

Talk soon,
Majo

13.title: A person I admire
13.brief: Describe a person who has influenced you. Use relative pronouns to give information about them.
13.briefEs: Describe a una persona que te ha influido usando pronombres relativos (who, that, which, whose).
criteria: Four relative clauses with who, that, which or whose.
Two participle adjectives (inspiring, impressed).
Include “reliable” or “to come across as”.
13.model: The person who has influenced me most is my aunt Gloria. She is a doctor that works in a small hospital in Chocó. She is a woman whose patience is amazing. At first she comes across as serious, but she is very funny. Her work, which is often exhausting, is very inspiring for me. I was really impressed when she saved a baby's life during a storm. She is the most reliable person I know. I want to be like her.

13.title: Lost and found
13.brief: You lost something important. Write a notice for the building or school notice board describing the object.
13.briefEs: Escribe un aviso para el tablero describiendo algo importante que perdiste.
criteria: Two relative clauses (a bag which has…, the person who finds it).
Use “broken” or another past participle as an adjective.
Include contact information and a polite request.
13.model:
LOST: BLACK BACKPACK
I lost a black backpack which has a small broken zip on the front. It contains a laptop that has a sticker of a cat, and a blue notebook whose pages are full of notes for my thesis. I lost it on Monday in the library. The person who finds it will get a reward! Please call or write to Juan: 311 456 7890. Thank you!

13.title: A fascinating documentary
13.brief: Write a review of a documentary or film you saw. Describe it and your feelings.
13.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de un documental o película que viste: descríbelo y cuenta cómo te sentiste.
criteria: Three -ing / -ed adjective forms used correctly.
Three relative clauses with who, that or which.
End with a recommendation.
13.model: I watched a documentary about the oceans last night, and I was fascinated. It's a film that shows animals which live very deep in the sea. The pictures are amazing, and the story is never boring. A scientist who works in Chile explains everything in a clear way. The only confusing part is the ending, so some people were confused. I was a bit tired after two hours, but it was an inspiring film. I recommend it to everyone who likes nature.

13.title: Who is your new teacher?
13.brief: Two students talk about a new teacher. Write a short conversation to identify and describe her.
13.briefEs: Dos estudiantes hablan de una profesora nueva. Escribe una conversación corta para identificarla y describirla.
criteria: Three relative clauses with who, whose and that.
One -ing adjective for a cause (boring).
A question “What’s she like?” with an answer.
13.model:
Who is your new teacher?
She's the woman who teaches Art.
What's she like?
She's very kind, and her classes are never boring.
Is she the one whose dog comes to school?
Yes! The dog that sleeps under her desk.

13.title: A reliable plumber
13.brief: A neighbour needs a plumber. Write a message to recommend one.
13.briefEs: Una vecina necesita un plomero. Escribe un mensaje para recomendar a uno.
criteria: Four relative clauses with who, that, which or whose.
Two participle adjectives (broken, impressive, annoyed).
Use “reliable” and “comes across as”.
13.model:
Hi Marta,

I know a plumber who is very reliable. His name is Ramón, and he fixed the broken pipe that flooded my kitchen. He arrived in twenty minutes, which was impressive. He's a man whose work is always clean, and he doesn't charge too much. He comes across as serious, but he's really friendly. The price was fair, so I wasn't annoyed. I'll send you his number, and you can tell him that I sent you!

Carlos

13.title: Things that annoy me on the bus
13.brief: Write a post about things that annoy you when you travel by bus.
13.briefEs: Escribe una publicación sobre cosas que te molestan cuando viajas en bus.
criteria: Three relative clauses with who, whose or which.
One -ing / -ed pair (annoying / annoyed).
Use “exhausted” and ask your readers a question.
13.model: Things that annoy me on the bus! First, people who play loud music without headphones. It's so annoying! Second, passengers whose bags take two seats. I get annoyed every day. Third, the driver who talks on the phone, which is also worrying. Last week, I was exhausted after work, and a man who was eating chips sat next to me. The smell was terrible! What annoys you? Tell me in the comments. #commuting

13.title: Volunteering at an animal shelter
13.brief: Write a diary entry about a day as a volunteer. Describe people, animals and your feelings.
13.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario sobre un día como voluntario: describe personas, animales y tus sentimientos.
criteria: Three relative clauses (who, that, whose).
Four -ing / -ed adjectives used correctly.
Use “in charge” and finish with a sentence about your feelings.
13.model:
Saturday, 21 September

Today I volunteered at an animal shelter, and it was exhausting but fascinating. The woman who is in charge gave me a job: I looked after a puppy that was frightened. I was surprised when he ate from my hand. Then a girl whose cat was lost came to the shelter, and she was very worried. The cat was found in the garden, so everyone was relieved! I'm exhausted now, but I'm really excited about next weekend.

13.title: What makes a good friend?
13.brief: Write your opinion about what makes a good friend. Define it with relative clauses.
13.briefEs: Escribe tu opinión sobre qué hace a un buen amigo, definiéndolo con cláusulas de relativo.
criteria: Four relative clauses with who, whose or that.
One participle adjective (-ed or -ing).
Open with a definition and close with “In my opinion”.
13.model: A good friend is someone who listens to you. I think the best friends are people who are honest, even when the truth is difficult. They are also reliable, so you can ask them for help. A friend whose advice is always honest is worth keeping. My best friend is the person that I call when I'm worried, and she never comes across as bored. In my opinion, that is what matters.

14.title: Rules of my house
14.brief: Write the rules for living in your house or for a guest staying with you. Use modals of permission, obligation and prohibition.
14.briefEs: Escribe las reglas de tu casa para un huésped usando modales de permiso, obligación y prohibición.
criteria: Use can / be allowed to for permission.
Use have to / must for obligation and mustn’t / not allowed to for prohibition.
Use “be supposed to” once.
14.model: Welcome to our house! Here are the rules. You can use the kitchen any time, and you're allowed to invite friends on weekends. You have to wash your dishes after eating. You must close the main door at night because the cat escapes. You aren't allowed to smoke inside. You mustn't play loud music after 10 p.m. because the neighbours complain. You're supposed to tell us if you come home very late. Enjoy your stay!

14.title: Where's my phone?
14.brief: You can't find your phone. Write a message to a friend guessing where it is. Use modals and adverbs of certainty.
14.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un amigo adivinando dónde está tu celular usando grados de certeza.
criteria: Use must, might, could and can’t for deduction.
Use two adverbs: probably, perhaps, definitely.
Include “evidence”, “to assume” or “unlikely”.
14.model: Hi Mafe, I can't find my phone! I'm writing from my laptop. It must be in your car, because I used it there last night. Or it might be in the restaurant. Perhaps I left it on the table. It can't be at home: I've looked everywhere! It's unlikely that someone took it. Can you check your car? I probably dropped it under the seat. Thanks!

14.title: Rules at my workplace
14.brief: Write an email to a friend comparing the rules at your work or school with the rules at his or hers.
14.briefEs: Escribe un correo comparando las reglas de tu trabajo o colegio con las de un amigo.
criteria: Four different modals of obligation / permission.
Use “prohibited” or “forbidden”.
One sentence of certainty (I'm sure / it's probably).
14.model:
Hi Juancho,

Your new job sounds strict! At my office the rules are more relaxed. We don't have to wear a suit — we're allowed to wear jeans every day. We can work from home on Fridays. But we have to arrive before 8:30, and phones are prohibited in meetings. We're supposed to have lunch in one hour, but nobody checks. At your company, are you allowed to work from home? It's probably difficult with so many rules!

Cheers,
Pipe

14.title: Where is Sofía?
14.brief: A classmate is missing. Write a short conversation where two friends guess where she is and give their evidence.
14.briefEs: Falta una compañera. Escribe una conversación corta en la que dos amigos adivinan dónde está y dan sus pruebas.
criteria: Use “must”, “can’t” and “might” or “could” for deductions.
Give evidence for two deductions.
Use “perhaps” or “probably” once.
14.model:
Where is Sofía? She isn't in class.
She must be ill. She had a cold yesterday.
She can't be at home. I saw her bag in the library.
Then she might be studying there.
Perhaps. She could be with the teacher, too.

14.title: May we use the hall?
14.brief: You are in a school club. Write an email to a teacher to ask for permission to use the school hall.
14.briefEs: Eres parte de un club del colegio. Escribe un correo a un profesor para pedir permiso de usar el salón de actos.
criteria: Ask permission with “May we…?” and “Are we allowed to…?”.
Use “supposed to” and “must” once each.
Formal greeting, reason and closing.
14.model:
Dear Mr Evans,

I am a member of the drama club, and I am writing to ask for permission. May we use the school hall on Thursday afternoon? We are supposed to practise for the end-of-term show, but our classroom is too small. We can finish by five o'clock. We know that we must leave the hall tidy. Are we allowed to use the stage lights? A teacher can be present if it is necessary. Thank you very much.

Yours sincerely,
Irene Walsh

14.title: Mystery object
14.brief: Post a photo of a strange object and ask your followers to guess what it is.
14.briefEs: Publica la foto de un objeto extraño y pide a tus seguidores que adivinen qué es.
criteria: Use must, can’t, might and could for deductions.
Two adverbs (perhaps, probably, definitely).
Give evidence with “because” and ask a question.
14.model: Can you guess what this is? Look at the photo! It must be a kitchen tool, because it has a handle. It can't be a toy because it's made of metal. It might be for cutting vegetables, or it could be for opening bottles. Perhaps it's very old. I definitely don't think it's a pen. My sister says it's probably a hammer, but I'm not certain. What do you think? #mysteryobject

14.title: My first week at camp
14.brief: Write a diary entry about your first week at a summer camp. Describe the rules and how you feel.
14.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario sobre tu primera semana en un campamento: las normas y cómo te sientes.
criteria: Use “have to”, “be allowed to”, “be supposed to” and “mustn’t” once each.
One “don’t have to”.
Personal feelings and a final plan.
14.model:
Friday night

What a week! At camp, we have to get up at seven, and we're not allowed to use our phones during the day. We're supposed to clean our rooms every morning, but my roommate forgets. We mustn't swim alone, so we always go with a guide. I don't have to cook, which is great! At first, I missed my family, but now I'm happy because there is so much to do. I think I'll stay another week if my parents allow it.

14.title: Social media for teenagers
14.brief: Give your opinion: should teenagers be allowed to use social media? Explain the rules.
14.briefEs: Da tu opinión: ¿deberían los adolescentes poder usar redes sociales? Explica las normas.
criteria: Use “be allowed to”, “must” and “mustn’t” once each.
One “don’t have to” and one “be supposed to”.
State your opinion at the beginning and at the end.
14.model: I think teenagers should be allowed to use social media, but there have to be some rules. Young people aren't allowed to open an account before they are thirteen, and I agree with that. They must keep their passwords secret, and they mustn't talk to strangers. Parents don't have to read every message, but they can check the privacy settings. Teenagers are supposed to be online for only two hours a day. In my opinion, trust is better than strict rules.

14.title: Who will win the final?
14.brief: Write a message to a friend about the school football final. Say who you think will win and why.
14.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un amigo sobre la final de fútbol del colegio: quién crees que ganará y por qué.
criteria: Use must, might, could and can’t.
Two adverbs of certainty (probably, perhaps, definitely).
A reason with “because” and a final question.
14.model:
Hi Tomás,

I think our team must be the favourite for the final. They have trained all month, so they can't be afraid. The other team might be fast, but we have a better goalkeeper. It could rain, and perhaps that will help us because we play well in the mud. The match probably starts at four, so you'd better come early. I definitely want to watch it with you. Is that OK?

Diego

15.title: If I won the lottery
15.brief: Write about what you would do if you won a lot of money. Use the second conditional.
15.briefEs: Escribe qué harías si te ganaras la lotería usando el segundo condicional.
criteria: Five second conditional sentences (If + past, would + verb).
Use “If I were…” once.
Use “instead of” or “otherwise”.
15.model: If I won the lottery, I would buy a house for my parents first. Then I would travel around the world for a year. I would visit Japan, Egypt and Peru. If I had a lot of money, I wouldn't stop working, but I would start my own company instead of working for a boss. I would also help a school in my town. If I were a millionaire, I would be careful, otherwise I would lose everything!

15.title: A decision I regret
15.brief: Write about a decision you made in the past that you regret. Say what you should have done and what would have happened.
15.briefEs: Escribe sobre una decisión que lamentas: qué deberías haber hecho y qué habría pasado.
criteria: Two sentences with “should have / shouldn’t have + past participle”.
Two sentences with “would have + past participle”.
Use “to regret”, “to turn down” or “in hindsight”.
15.model: Three years ago, I was offered a job in Spain, but I turned it down because I was afraid. I regret it now. I should have accepted the offer. I shouldn't have listened to my fears. In hindsight, it would have been a great experience. I would have learned a lot and I would have met people from different countries. But I learned a lesson: next time I'll say yes to new opportunities, even if they scare me.

15.title: Advice in your shoes
15.brief: A friend wrote: “My boss is unfair and I want to quit, but I need the money.” Write a reply with advice using “If I were you…”.
15.briefEs: Responde a un amigo con un problema en el trabajo con consejos usando “If I were you…”.
criteria: Use “If I were you / In your shoes, I would…”.
Three second conditional sentences.
One past modal: should have or would have.
15.model:
Hi Jaime,

I'm sorry about your boss. If I were you, I wouldn't quit right now. In your shoes, I would look for another job first. If you talked to the HR department, they might help you. If I had a boss like that, I would write down every problem. Maybe you should have complained earlier, but it's not too late. Don't blame yourself!

Take care,
Silvia

15.title: What would you do?
15.brief: Two friends ask each other what they would do in an imaginary situation. Write a short conversation.
15.briefEs: Dos amigos se preguntan qué harían en una situación imaginaria. Escribe una conversación corta.
criteria: Two second conditional sentences or questions (If + past, would + verb).
One contraction with ’d (I’d call).
A short reaction (That’s a good idea).
15.model:
What would you do if you found a wallet?
I would take it to the police. What about you?
I'd look for a name inside. If there was a phone number, I'd call it.
That's a good idea. I wouldn't keep the money.

15.title: If I were the mayor
15.brief: Write a post about what you would change if you were the mayor of your city.
15.briefEs: Escribe una publicación sobre qué cambiarías si fueras el alcalde de tu ciudad.
criteria: Four second conditional sentences, none with “would” after “if”.
Use “If I were…” once.
Ask your followers a second conditional question.
15.model: If I were the mayor of my city, I would build more parks. I would also make the buses free for students, because many families couldn't pay for transport. If I had more money, I would plant a thousand trees. I wouldn't allow cars in the city centre on Sundays. If people could walk safely, they would be happier. What would you change if you were in charge? #mycity

15.title: I'm sorry, I should have called
15.brief: You forgot a friend's party. Write a message to apologise and explain what you should have done.
15.briefEs: Olvidaste la fiesta de una amiga. Escribe un mensaje para disculparte y explicar qué deberías haber hecho.
criteria: Two sentences with “should have / shouldn’t have + past participle”.
Two sentences with “would have” or “could have” + past participle.
Use “regret” and a promise.
15.model:
Hi Valeria,

I'm really sorry about yesterday. I should have called you before the party, and I shouldn't have forgotten your invitation. If I had checked my phone, I would have seen your message. I would have come earlier if I had known the time. You could have texted me again, but I understand why you were angry. I regret my mistake. Could we have lunch tomorrow? I promise I will be on time.

Gabi

15.title: A concert that could have been better
15.brief: Write a review of a concert that was disappointing. Say what should have been different.
15.briefEs: Escribe una reseña de un concierto decepcionante: qué debería haber sido diferente.
criteria: Three sentences with “should have” or “would have” + past participle.
One second conditional (I would go if…).
Use “in hindsight” once.
15.model: Last night's concert was disappointing. The band should have started at eight, but they arrived at nine. The organisers should have told us about the delay. We would have gone home earlier if we had known. If the sound had been better, I would have enjoyed the music more. The singer was excellent, though. I wouldn't pay forty pounds again, but I would go if the tickets were cheaper. In hindsight, we should have bought tickets for the other show.

15.title: If school started later
15.brief: Give your opinion about what would happen if school started later.
15.briefEs: Da tu opinión sobre qué pasaría si las clases empezaran más tarde.
criteria: Four second conditional sentences (If + past, would / could + verb).
Use “wouldn’t” once and “could” once.
End with an opinion sentence.
15.model: I think students would learn more if school started later. If we slept for nine hours, we wouldn't be so tired in the morning. We could concentrate better, and teachers would see better results. If lessons began at nine, many families would have problems with work times, but they could change their routines. I wouldn't mind finishing at five if I had more sleep. In my opinion, a later start would be worth it.

15.title: A complaint to an airline
15.brief: Your suitcase did not arrive when you flew from Bogotá to Madrid. Write a formal complaint to the airline.
15.briefEs: Tu maleta no llegó en un vuelo de Bogotá a Madrid. Escribe una queja formal a la aerolínea.
criteria: Two sentences with “should have / shouldn’t have + past participle”.
One third conditional and one second conditional.
A formal greeting, a clear request and a closing.
15.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about my flight from Bogotá to Madrid on 14 July. My suitcase did not arrive, and nobody explained the problem to me. The staff should have told us where to go, and they shouldn't have left us waiting for two hours. If I had known about the problem, I would have bought clothes at the airport. I would have felt better if somebody had offered help. I'm now in Madrid without my things. If you paid for my new clothes, I would be satisfied. I would like an answer within ten days.

Yours faithfully,
Camila Torres

16.title: What did they say?
16.brief: You went to a meeting and your colleague missed it. Write a message reporting what people said and asked.
16.briefEs: Escribe un mensaje a un colega que faltó a una reunión reportando lo que dijeron.
criteria: Four reported statements with backshift (said that she was…).
Two reported requests or commands (told us to…, asked us not to…).
Use “tell” with a person and “say” without.
16.model: Hi Andrés, you missed the meeting! The boss said that the company was opening a new office in Cali. She told us that sales were going up. Mario said he wanted to move to the new office. The boss asked us to send our reports by Friday. She also told us not to use the meeting room on Monday. Oh, and she said she would buy pizza for everyone next week!

16.title: A message from the doctor
16.brief: You went to the doctor. Write an email to a friend reporting what the doctor said and told you to do.
16.briefEs: Escribe un correo a un amigo reportando lo que el médico te dijo y te pidió hacer.
criteria: Three reported statements (She said that I had…).
Three reported commands with told me to / not to.
Include “to insist”, “to remind” or “apparently”.
16.model:
Hi Nati,

I went to the doctor today because of my back. She said that I had a small problem with a muscle. Apparently, I sit too much at work. She told me to walk for thirty minutes every day and she told me not to carry heavy bags. She insisted that I needed to sleep more, too. She reminded me to take the pills after meals. She said I would feel better in a week.

Love,
Caro

16.title: The interview
16.brief: Write about a job interview (real or invented). Report the interviewer's questions, statements and your answers.
16.briefEs: Relata una entrevista de trabajo reportando las preguntas, afirmaciones y tus respuestas.
criteria: Two reported questions (She asked me where I lived / if I…).
Two reported statements and one reported command.
Use two reporting verbs: mention, admit, promise, point out.
16.model: Last week I had an interview at a travel agency. The manager asked me why I wanted the job. I told her that I loved travelling and helping people. She asked me if I spoke other languages. I admitted that my French wasn't very good. She pointed out that most clients spoke English, so it wasn't a problem. Then she told me to wait outside. After ten minutes, she said I could start on Monday. I promised I would work hard.

16.title: After the lesson
16.brief: Two classmates talk after a lesson about what the teacher said. Write a short conversation using reported speech.
16.briefEs: Dos compañeros hablan después de clase sobre lo que dijo la profesora. Escribe una conversación corta con estilo indirecto.
criteria: Two reported statements with backshift (said that… was).
One reported command (told us not to…).
One reported question with “if” (asked me if I was…).
16.model:
What did the teacher say?
She said that the test was on Friday.
Did she tell us to bring a dictionary?
No, she told us not to bring anything.
She asked me if I was ready.
What did you answer?
I said that I wasn't sure.

16.title: What my grandmother told me
16.brief: Write a diary entry about a conversation with your grandmother about her childhood. Report what she said.
16.briefEs: Escribe una entrada de diario sobre una conversación con tu abuela sobre su infancia, reportando lo que dijo.
criteria: Four reported statements with backshift.
One reported question with “if”.
One reported command or advice (told me to…) and the verb “promised”.
16.model:
Sunday

Today my grandmother told me about her childhood. She said that she was born in a small village near Cuenca. She told me that her family didn't have a car, so they walked everywhere. She said that she used to help her mother at the market. I asked her if she liked school. She answered that she loved it, but she had to leave when she was twelve. She told me to study hard because education was important. I promised that I would.

16.title: A message pad at reception
16.brief: You work at a hotel reception. Complete the message pad for a guest, reporting what a caller said and asked.
16.briefEs: Trabajas en la recepción de un hotel. Completa la hoja de mensajes para un huésped, reportando lo que dijo y pidió quien llamó.
criteria: Two reported statements (said that…), one with “would”.
One reported request (asked me to…) and one negative (told me not to…).
One reported question with “if” and one verb like “insisted”.
16.model: Mr Lopez called at ten this morning. He said that he was at the airport and that his flight was delayed. He asked me to tell you that he would arrive at three. He also asked if you could book a taxi. He told me not to call his mobile because the battery was low. He insisted that the meeting should start without him. Please call him at the hotel tonight.

16.title: The rumour
16.brief: Write a short story about a rumour at school and how it changed as people repeated it.
16.briefEs: Escribe una historia corta sobre un rumor en el colegio y cómo cambió al repetirse.
criteria: Four reported statements or questions with correct backshift.
Use “apparently” and “mention” or “remind”.
Two reported requests (told us not to…, reminded us to…).
16.model: On Monday, Carla told me that the school was going to close the library. She said that she had heard it from Ben. I asked Ben if it was true, but he said that he hadn't said that. Apparently, the director had only mentioned a short repair. Everyone had changed the story a little. In the end, the librarian told us not to believe rumours. She reminded us to ask the teachers first.

16.title: Funny things my cousin says
16.brief: Write a post about funny things a child said today. Report his or her words.
16.briefEs: Escribe una publicación sobre cosas graciosas que dijo hoy un niño, reportando sus palabras.
criteria: Four reporting verbs (told, said, asked, promised).
Correct backshift in each reported statement.
One reported question with “if” and one reported request (asked her to…).
16.model: My little cousin Tomás is five, and he says funny things! This morning he told me that he wanted to be a dinosaur. He said that dinosaurs didn't have homework. Then he asked me if I could fly. I said that I couldn't, and he looked disappointed. At lunch, he told my aunt that the soup was too hot, and he asked her to blow on it. He also promised that he would eat all his vegetables. We'll see! #kids

16.title: Customer comments
16.brief: You are a waiter. Write an email to the manager with a summary of what customers said and asked today.
16.briefEs: Eres mesero. Escribe un correo a la gerente con un resumen de lo que dijeron y pidieron los clientes hoy.
criteria: Four reported statements or questions with backshift.
Three different reporting verbs (complained, insisted, admitted…).
One reported request (asked me to…) and one reported question (asked if…).
16.model:
Dear Mrs Reyes,

Here is a summary of today's comments. A guest at table four told me that the soup was cold, and she asked me to bring a new one. Two students said that the music was too loud. One man complained that he had waited for forty minutes, and he insisted on speaking to you. A family asked if we had a children's menu. Everyone admitted that the dessert was excellent. Could you tell me what I should say tomorrow?

Best wishes,
Nico
